Figure 3C plots the Cooperation GAP against the Social Rank GAP for non-friends, mutual friends, and sender-declared one-sided friendships. Solid curves use observed transfers; semi-transparent curves use null-model-filtered transfers.

# Build the child and interval summaries

For each child and friendship group, the descriptive GAP is mean tokens received minus mean tokens sent. Children are grouped into seven equal-width intervals of their median Social Rank GAP. Each plotted point averages the finite child-level GAPs in its interval. The code below builds these summaries directly from the prepared dyad data, so this page can be run after [Data and measures](01_data_and_measures.qmd) without executing either preceding figure page. The loading step prepares missing inputs automatically.

# Observed and filtered support

With observed transfers, every child's sent and received means use the same partners. The mean child-level Cooperation GAP therefore equals the difference between the two mean curves in [Figure 3B](06_figure3b_tokens_by_rank.qmd).

With filtered transfers, each direction uses its own retained allocations. A child may have a sent mean, a received mean, both, or neither. `dif_coop` is finite only when both means exist, and the plotted filtered GAP averages those finite child-level differences. Consequently, the filtered GAP need not equal the difference between separately averaged sent and received curves. This descriptive construction also differs from the filtered regressions, which require both transfers of each pair to be retained.

```{r inspect-filtered-support}
#| code-summary: "inspect-filtered-support"
children %>%
  filter(version == "Filtered") %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(n_children = n(),
            n_valid_sent = sum(is.finite(sent)),
            n_valid_received = sum(is.finite(received)),
            n_valid_coop_gap = sum(is.finite(dif_coop)),
            .groups = "drop")
```

For each interval, `n` counts all children and `n_with_value` counts finite child-level GAPs. The displayed interval half-width `se_dif_coop` is computed as $1.96\,SD/\sqrt{n}$ using the total interval count. The plotting table exposes both counts so that support can be inspected directly.

```{r inspect-gap-support}
#| code-summary: "inspect-gap-support"
binned %>%
  select(group, version, round_gap, median_gap, n, n_with_value, mean_dif_coop, se_dif_coop)
```
